articles.title: Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India's First LED Curved-Dome Facility - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India’s First LED Curved-Dome Facility Breaking News Mysuru Planetarium Opens as India’s First LED Curved-Dome Facility By Maria Dsouza November 14, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Mysuru planetarium described as India’s first LED curved-dome planetarium, along with the Cosmos–Mysuru cosmology education and research training centre, at the foothills of Chamundi Hill on Friday. The facilities have been built by the Union Department of Science and Technology and are intended to expand public access to astronomy education and research training. Speaking at a public function after the inauguration, Modi said science and innovation were being consistently encouraged to support society and development. He described the planetarium as a new chapter in India’s scientific journey and said it could help give shape to the aspirations of young people. The Prime Minister visited the planetarium and was briefed on its advanced facilities. He also viewed space-related presentations from the facility’s “Sky Theatre” and interacted with children. Describing the experience as “truly wonderful”, Modi said a visit to the planetarium could turn people’s attention towards the sky and encourage them to understand the wider universe and its unanswered questions. The project combines a public-facing astronomy venue with the Cosmos–Mysuru centre, which is focused on cosmology education and research training. The source report does not specify the total project cost, seating capacity, operating schedule or the number of students and visitors the facility is expected to serve. At the event, Modi linked the new facility to Mysuru’s longer educational history. He referred to the establishment of the University of Mysore during the period of Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the role of the Wadiyar family in the establishment of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. He said these institutions had provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to develop their abilities and pursue new work. The Prime Minister also highlighted the government’s decision to open the space sector to private participation, saying this had created new opportunities for private industry and a platform for Indian start-ups to demonstrate their capabilities. He said satellite technology, space science and earth-science technologies were being combined to improve everyday life. Research access was another theme of the address. Modi said students and researchers needed access to high-quality research facilities and scientific publications, and referred to the One Nation One Subscription initiative as a measure launched for that purpose. The report does not provide further operational details about how the initiative will be linked to the Cosmos–Mysuru centre. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Governor Sudha Yadav, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddi and Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar attended the programme. The new planetarium adds a specialised science-education facility to Mysuru’s institutional landscape, while its longer public impact will depend on access, programming and the scale of its engagement with schools, students and researchers. articles.title: PM Modi dedicates India's first LED dome planetarium in Mysuru - Dailyhunt
articles.content: M ysuru : Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, November 13, dedicated COSMOS Planetarium, India's first LED Dome Planetarium, to the nation, describing it as a major addition to the country's scientific infrastructure that would inspire young minds to explore the mysteries of the universe and contribute to India's growing achievements in science and technology. Advertisement Speaking at the inauguration, Modi said the state-of-the-art facility would open new opportunities for students, researchers and young enthusiasts to develop scientific curiosity, deepen their understanding of astronomy and pursue new discoveries. He described COSMOS as a new chapter in India’s scientific journey and called for greater participation by school and college students. The Prime Minister said the planetarium would provide an immersive experience of the universe and help young people develop an interest in scientific exploration. He also congratulated the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various government departments and all those associated with the project. Modi said he had the opportunity to watch a show at the planetarium and described the experience as extraordinary. Spirituality and science share India’s heritage Drawing a parallel between COSMOS Planetarium and Viveka Smaraka, which he had inaugurated in Mysuru recently, Modi said the two institutions conveyed an important message about India’s traditions of spirituality and scientific inquiry. While Viveka Smaraka encouraged people to look within themselves and seek spiritual knowledge, COSMOS invited them to look towards the skies and understand the vastness of the universe. “India’s traditions of spirituality and science have always progressed together,” he said. Recalling India’s historical contributions to astronomy, Modi referred to ancient scholars such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Neelakantha Somayaji. He said these mathematicians and astronomers had made significant discoveries and carried out complex calculations at a time when modern scientific instruments and technologies were not available. Their achievements reflected the country’s longstanding tradition of scientific thinking and intellectual inquiry, he said. The Prime Minister also highlighted Mysuru’s contribution to education and research. He recalled that the University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and that the Wadiyar family had played an important role in laying the foundation for the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. These institutions had created opportunities for generations of students, researchers and academics, strengthening Karnataka’s contribution to India’s educational and scientific development. Indian students making their mark internationally Highlighting the achievements of young Indians in science, Modi referred to the country’s performance at international Olympiads and competitions. He said five Indian students had participated in the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics held in Vietnam this year. Four of them won gold medals, while one secured a silver medal. Indian students had also achieved record success in international Olympiads in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology, winning gold and silver medals. The facility has been developed as a centre for cosmology education and research training. The inauguration places a new science-focused public facility within Mysuru’s established educational and cultural landscape. According to Prajavani, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman briefed the Prime Minister about the planetarium during the event. Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddy were among those present. Their participation brought together the Union government, the state administration and the higher education department at the opening of the facility. The planetarium’s LED curved-dome format is the central technological feature identified in the report. Its stated purpose extends beyond public viewing: Cosmos-Mysuru is intended to support cosmology education and research training, linking science communication with institutional learning. The facility is located near Chamundi Hill, an important landmark and visitor destination in Mysuru. Its opening adds a science and education venue to an area already associated with the city’s public identity and tourism activity. The report does not provide details on the planetarium’s construction cost, capacity, operating schedule, exhibits or access arrangements. The inauguration marks the beginning of the facility’s public and educational role. Further information on its programmes, visitor operations and research-training activities will determine how the new planetarium is integrated into Mysuru’s education and science outreach network.
